title: with expressions and immutability
hook: Under high concurrency, copy a policy record with with and hand the snapshot to the worker. Do not mutate a shared scoring object while 999 submits land.

sections.heading: Records, copy, with
sections.prose: A record (class or struct) gives you value-based equality, a Deconstruct, and a copy constructor. with uses that copy constructor, then assigns the properties you name. The original instance is unchanged. init-only properties are settable during with. Ordinary classes do not get with unless you provide the copy machinery yourself. record struct copies the struct; there is no extra heap object unless nested references exist.

snippets.label: Snapshot a scoring policy for a submit burst
snippets.explanation: Each submit path reads frozen. Updating live later does not change in-flight copies. That is the immutability bargain.

sections.heading: Shallow copy is the trap
sections.prose: If a record contains a List<string> of allowed LMS domains, with copies the reference. Mutating that list from two attempts is still a race. Nested records can be nested with expressions. For collections, prefer immutable types or copy the list explicitly in the with initializer. Pattern matching pairs with with: match a policy, then produce the next state as a new record instead of setting fields.

snippets.label: Nested with plus a copied list
snippets.explanation: Collection expressions copy into a new list. consumer.Audiences.Add(audience) would mutate the shared list and defeat with.

interviewTakeaways: with copies a record (or copyable struct) and sets named properties.
The copy is shallow; nested mutable collections stay shared.
Use snapshots for concurrent attempt-submit instead of locking field writes on a live object.
Ordinary classes do not support with by default.
commonPitfalls: Calling with and then mutating a nested List on the new instance.
Assuming record equality compares nested lists by value — List equality is referential unless you customize.
Using with on a class and expecting a compiler error to be the only issue — it simply does not compile.

jsTsCorrelations.note: const next = { ...live, allowLate: false } is a shallow copy, same trap as with. JS has no compiler-generated value equality on that object.
